newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila sugar millers say continue US sugar exports.
newsitem.headline: Manila sugar millers say continue US sugar exports.

text.p: The Philippine Sugar Millers Association said on Monday the country should continue to export sugar to the United States despite a shortfall in the domestic market.

"The Philippines has enjoyed the better end of the deal for every nine out of ten years ... and it would be in the best interest of the Philippines to retain the U.S. quota," the millers said in a statement.
The Philippine government is considering stopping the exports to the U.S. because of a shortfall which has forced the country to import for its own needs.

The U.S., in order to help some countries, imports sugar under fixed quotas at a premium over market prices. The U.S. quota offers the Philippines a price of 22 cents a pound regardless of prevailing market prices. Raw sugar in the world market is currently at 11 cents per pound.

Recently, Sugar Regulatory Administration chief Wilson Gamboa said the Philippines should stop exporting sugar to the United States because the benefits were reaped by just a section of the sugar industry.
